cells.tense: You are at the bench with the work in front of you, taking away what doesn't hold, and the cut is good.
cells.act: deepen the mastery by persisting at it
cells.ask: Give the piece you're refining today's pass. Same hour tomorrow, and the day after, with no finish line in view.
cells.core:
You can tell what holds from what doesn't, and you do it alone, without an audience, by sitting with a piece until the false part gives itself up. Kept at, this turns into mastery — not one good pass but the same pass returned to slowly, for as long as it takes.

What makes it deepen instead of run dry is returning on ordinary days when nothing depends on the result. Give the work today's pass, then tomorrow's, then the day after. The repetition is the point; it's how a good ear becomes a reliable one. You'll learn the difference between a line that held and a line you let slide, and that knowledge lives only in hands that came back. The mastery isn't a talent you're proving; it's something you keep, and it feeds itself.
cells.sheetLine: You return on plain days, and the work deepens.
cells.verb: cutting what matters from what doesn't until the line is true
cells.place: a room where you keep adjusting the mix until the sound is right

cells.tense: You are holding tomorrow's test against what you haven't made yet, and the blade gets thinner than the work needs.
cells.act: let what you gave up be seen by the people it was for, without a word about it
cells.ask: Let whoever this practice costs see the given-up hours — and stay quiet about why it was worth it.
cells.core:
Your eye runs past the work into what isn't built yet. You test distinctions no one asked for, keep the passes private, and the pressure has nowhere to land except back on you. What was sharp starts to feel like strain, because nothing you finish is finished enough for an eye that keeps moving.

What's thin here isn't precision. It's being seen. Let the people this practice is for stand near the cost of it — the hours, what you set down to keep going — and don't explain that it was worth it. What was given up, simply visible, becomes something they can hold too. The pressure stops being yours alone. The next pass gets easier. So does stopping for the night.
cells.sheetLine: You're testing tomorrow's blade before today has one.

cells.tense: Something you used to test carefully got decided a while back, and you haven't picked it up again.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: Accept what someone offers you, offer something back at the same size, and keep no tally of it.
cells.core:
The private testing isn't running. You land on a judgment and stop there; the return, the willingness to find out you were wrong, has gone quiet. From outside it can look like clear opinions, but what made them worth having was the going-back. A verdict has taken the place of a practice.

What wakes it up is exchange with someone. Accept what's offered, offer something back at the same size, and don't keep score. Not a favor you'll collect, not a debt owed. Someone offers, you take it; you offer, they take it. That two-way movement is the ground the quiet work stands on. Do it once this week and the practice has somewhere to land that isn't only your own head.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped testing and started holding the verdict.

cells.tense: You've been weighing true against false so long you'd call it just how you are.
cells.act: eat the meal you made and leave the kitchen as it is
cells.ask: Eat the meal you cooked, exactly as it is. Don't fix the seasoning. Don't clean up yet.
cells.core:
You don't count the weighing as a choice anymore. It looks like good taste you happen to have, not a practice you kept, alone, before anyone could see what you were doing. The eye is yours. The hours behind it are yours.

Before you were refining things, you were someone who imagined them. Let that come back. Eat the meal you made and leave the kitchen as it is: no extra salt, no wiping the counter, no improving the plate. What sits under the weighing is the imagining, also yours, and it's been waiting for you to stop fixing and stand where the finished thing is, full as it is.
cells.sheetLine: It isn't your nature. It's work you did and didn't sign.

attempts.check: The record says the Honing capacity is private, inner, Body-Bridge through Air; it does not say the person keeps their sharp seeing hidden from anyone, only that the work is personal. A reader could object that they show their thinking all the time, and the Unacknowledged cell should survive that by pointing at authorship rather than secrecy. The asks stay useful if the read is wrong: each one is a small act the person can do or skip, and none depends on the diagnosis holding. The sentence that serves me more than them is the Tune poetry about 'calibration'; I've kept that out of the asks and kept one plain image in the Unacknowledged core, carried through.
